title: AliExpress has lost it's magic
text:
AliExpress has lost it's magic
I've been using AliExpress since 2014, and it was my first choice for electronic components, and small household items. However a number of selling practices have been introduced recently that really put the customer on the back foot. 
Many items are now advertised as Free shipping over ￡8.00, but cost less than £8 and only show a Max. 1 pcs/shopper so you never get the free shipping and are unable to bundle the item.
Also many  items are displayed at a cheap price, but when you click onto the item, it turns out that the cheap price refers to something else, so is not the real price.
Both of these practices really detract from the shopping experience, I have now switched over to e-bay for some of my shopping.

title: I had a very disappointing experience…
text:
I had a very disappointing experience with AliExpress.

I ordered a bag, but they delivered the wrong item while I was away from home. As soon as I returned, I contacted customer service and explained the situation. They asked me to provide photos and videos as evidence, which I did. Despite submitting everything they requested, they later responded that I had not provided “valid evidence” and closed my case without resolving the issue or offering a refund or replacement.

As a customer, I feel this was unfair. If the evidence they requested was not sufficient, they should have clearly explained what additional proof was needed instead of simply closing the case.

Based on my experience, I encourage buyers to be cautious when ordering from AliExpress. If something goes wrong with your order, don’t assume you’ll receive fair support. My experience has left me feeling disappointed and without confidence in their customer service.

I have been an online shopper for many years and have used both AliExpress and Temu. Unfortunately, my recent experience with AliExpress has been extremely disappointing.

I specifically ordered a **blue bag** because I did not want a black one. The seller sent me what is clearly a **black bag**, not the colour I ordered.

I submitted multiple return requests and provided photos showing the item I received. Each time, AliExpress rejected my request, saying my photos were "insufficient proof," despite the issue being that the product delivered did not match what I ordered.

What is most frustrating is that this isn't simply a case of changing my mind. I received an item that differs from what I purchased, yet I have still been unable to obtain the advertised free return.

In contrast, I have shopped with Temu for years and have had consistently straightforward experiences when using their free return policy. If an item is incorrect or doesn't meet expectations, the return process has been simple and hassle-free.

Based on my experience, I no longer have confidence in AliExpress's advertised Free Return policy. If you are considering buying from AliExpress because you believe the Free Return promise will protect you, I encourage you to carefully consider the potential difficulties if something goes wrong.

I hope AliExpress improves its dispute resolution process so that customers who receive items that do not match their orders can resolve the issue fairly and without unnecessary frustration.

title: Fake Sterling Silver Jewlery Almost Got Arrested For Aliexpress Incompitence Leaving Seller Sell Fake Products
text:
I am writing this review to warn other consumers about my experience with AliExpress.

I purchased a chain advertised as 925 Sterling Silver for approximately €85. I also paid import VAT and customs charges when it entered Cyprus because I believed I was purchasing genuine sterling silver jewellery.

When I later took the chain to a professional jeweller and pawnbroker, I was informed that the item was not genuine 925 sterling silver and had no precious metal value. The situation became so serious that the police were called because jewellery falsely represented as precious metal raises obvious concerns. After I explained that I had bought it from AliExpress believing it was genuine, I was allowed to leave without any action being taken against me.

From that moment, I expected AliExpress to protect its customer. Instead, I received generic responses, was told about buyer protection time limits, and was even asked to upload evidence to Google Drive rather than having the item professionally examined.

I have repeatedly asked AliExpress and the seller to:

Provide proof that the chain is genuine 925 sterling silver.
Produce any certificate of authenticity or assay report supporting the "925" claim.
Arrange and pay for tracked shipping so the chain can be sent to AliExpress headquarters or an independent laboratory for testing.
Refund my purchase, reimburse my import costs, and take responsibility if the item is proven not to be sterling silver.

Instead of answering these requests directly, my case has simply been passed between departments. It is now being investigated under Case No. 2053808477177295.

In my opinion, this experience demonstrates a serious failure of consumer protection. A marketplace that allows products to be advertised as precious metal should be able to verify those claims when challenged.

I trusted AliExpress, paid approximately €85 for what was advertised as genuine sterling silver, and ended up with an item that, according to the professional who examined it, is not sterling silver.

Until AliExpress either proves the authenticity of the product or fully compensates me, I cannot recommend buying jewellery or precious metals through this platform.

I will update this review once AliExpress reaches a final decision.

title: Poor after-sales support when a defective product is delivered
text:
I purchased a hair brush through AliExpress and unfortunately received a defective product.

I understand that manufacturing defects can happen with any company. My disappointment is not with the defect itself, but with how AliExpress handles these situations.

The only solutions offered were:

accept a small partial refund and keep a defective product; or
package the item myself, travel to a post office, and complete the entire return process in order to receive a full refund.

The issue is not the product's value (around US$10). The issue is the principle.

As a good-faith customer, I fulfilled my part of the contract: I selected the product, paid for it, and waited for delivery. The defective product was entirely the seller's responsibility. Nevertheless, AliExpress transferred the burden of solving the problem to me, requiring me to spend my own time and effort on a return process that I never agreed to when I made the purchase.

When everything goes well, delivery is made to my home. When something goes wrong because of the supplier, I'm expected to become part of their reverse logistics operation.

I find this policy unfair and contrary to what good customer service should look like. I expected AliExpress to take responsibility for resolving a problem it caused, instead of transferring the inconvenience to the customer.

I hope the company reviews this policy and adopts a more customer-friendly approach in cases where defective products are delivered.

I’ve been going in circles with AliExpress support for over a month now, and I’m writing this because at this point nothing else has worked.

The short version: I returned an item and paid for the return shipping myself, on the express understanding that it would be refunded. That wasn’t me assuming anything. Before the package even reached the seller, support told me in chat to keep the proof of payment because the shipping would be refunded once the return was complete. The return form in the app said the same. And the shipping cost was almost as much as the item itself, so if anyone had told me it was on me, I’d never have sent it back. It wouldn’t have been worth it.

Then it just became a wall.

July 7, they confirmed in writing: the shipping fee would be refunded based on the receipt. July 8, I sent the receipt, and there’s a logged reply on their side proving it. July 9, they closed the case saying they never got a valid response. That’s simply not true, and their own system shows it.

After that their escalation team offered a coupon as the refund format, and confirmed it twice, once on July 14. Issued within 1 to 5 business days if I replied within 24 hours. I replied on July 15, inside their own deadline. The coupon never showed up in my account. Not once. What I got instead was another email telling me no refund was possible at all.

So they promised, ignored my reply, closed the case for “silence,” then offered a coupon themselves, I accepted, and now it’s suddenly impossible. Every step of that is documented in their own emails.

What actually gets me isn’t even the money. It’s the lying. Different agents, same recycled lines, and a written promise from their own senior team that they’re now pretending never happened. A month of that.

If you’re reading this while deciding whether to buy from them: keep every screenshot, don’t trust a verbal or chat promise, and know that “we’ll refund it” can quietly turn into “policy says no” the moment the item’s back with the seller.

I still just want the coupon they already promised me in writing. That’s all.

AliExpress has ignored my evidence, wasted my time, and refuses to take responsibility for their own error. I demand a full refund of 35,49€ for shipping costs caused by their mistake.
UPDATE (28.07.2026): AliExpress responded asking for a return label and product inspection report. This is impossible — the product was already returned in October 2025 and rejected by Chinese customs due to AliExpress incorrect return instructions. title: The Worst Online Shopping Experience…
text:
The Worst Online Shopping Experience I’ve Ever Had

This has been, without question, the worst online shopping experience I have ever had.

The air conditioner I received arrived damaged. I immediately reported the issue, expecting the platform to protect the buyer when an item arrives defective.

Instead, I was repeatedly asked to return a very large and heavy item by self-shipping. I explained multiple times that I have health limitations and live alone, making it physically impossible for me to transport it. None of this was taken into consideration.

Customer service kept promising that my case would be escalated, but nothing ever changed. I spent hours contacting support, repeating the same explanation to different agents, only to receive the same scripted responses. In one case, an agent kept me waiting for a long time while supposedly working on my case, and the chat was automatically closed by the system for “no response” even though I was actively waiting.

I even tried to reach a reasonable solution with the seller, but the seller refused to cooperate. Instead of holding the seller accountable for shipping a damaged product, AliExpress placed the entire burden on me.

After shopping on many online marketplaces over the years, I have never experienced customer service this frustrating. This experience has completely destroyed my confidence in buying from AliExpress again.

My advice to anyone purchasing expensive or heavy items is simple think twice before ordering. If something goes wrong, don’t assume the platform will stand behind you.



Update:

AliExpress responded to my review and requested my order information, which I provided. However, several days have passed and I still have not received any actual solution or resolution.

This issue has already been ongoing for more than a month. I contacted the seller and AliExpress Customer Service multiple times, but the response has always been that the case would be escalated or reviewed by another team. Despite these repeated promises, no practical solution has been provided.

The original problem remains the same. The item arrived damaged, and I am still being asked to return a heavy damaged air conditioning unit at my own expense before receiving a refund.

I appreciate the response, but a response alone does not resolve the issue. I am still waiting for a fair and reasonable solution.



Update

AliExpress has responded again after my previous update. Unfortunately, instead of providing a practical solution, they are now asking me to submit an unboxing video showing the package being opened and the item inside, along with a damage report from the local shipping company.

This request comes long after the package was delivered and opened. It is impossible to recreate an unboxing video after the package has already been unpacked. I have already submitted clear photos showing the damaged air conditioner and have fully cooperated throughout this process for more than a month.

Below is the key part of AliExpress’s latest response

“We kindly ask you to provide the following

• A video of the unboxing process
• A damage report issued by your local logistics provider

Once we receive these materials, we will review the details and arrange an appropriate solution.”

I believe this demonstrates why my case remains unresolved. I have provided all the evidence that is reasonably available, yet I continue to receive requests for evidence that cannot realistically be produced after delivery.

I will continue updating this review with any further developments.

title: What I wish I'd known before buying cycling clothing from AliExpress.
text:
I purchased three items of cycling clothing from AliExpress for almost NZ$200. For varying reasons the items were unsuitable and not what I expected.The fabric quality was generally good, but the after-sales experience and dispute process were extremely disappointing. 
Here's what I wish I'd known before ordering.
1. Don't assume the published size guide is accurate.
I ordered one jersey according to the seller's published body measurements. My chest and waist measurements fell within the advertised size range, yet the jersey was significantly too small to wear. I supplied evidence of my body measurements + the seller's size chart and measurements of the actual garment, but my claim was rejected (no valid reason given).
2. Product photos don't always tell the full story.
A second cycling jersey looked excellent online, but the rear pockets were positioned much higher than every other well-fitting cycling jersey that I own. Rear pockets are an essential functional feature for cyclists. Their high-up-the-back position made them difficult and impractical to access while riding. I supplied comparison photographs and measurements to demonstrate the difference. Their response was the standard:- Your request was closed as the supporting information you provided was not sufficient.
3. Check that the product you receive actually matches the listing.
A thermal cycling vest was advertised with three rear pockets, but the vest I received had no rear pockets at all. I provided photographs and screenshots of the listing to demonstrate the difference.
4. Expect to provide extensive evidence if something goes wrong.
I supplied photographs, measurements, screenshots, comparison images and detailed written explanations for every dispute. Be prepared to document everything from the moment your parcel arrives.
5. Don't expect the dispute process to explain its decisions.
My disputes and appeals were repeatedly rejected with generic statements that my evidence was "insufficient", but without explaining why or addressing the specific evidence I had submitted. My evidence clearly demonstrated the issue. This left me with the impression that my submissions had not been truly considered. 
6. Returning an item is not as straightforward as it sounds.
AliExpress eventually agreed that I could return the vest, but only after paying international return postage to China upfront (which is almost as much as the cost of item itself). Although the seller is stated to be responsible for return shipping where an item is not as described, there was no clear or reliable assurance that I would be reimbursed in cash. The guidance also refers to reimbursement by AliExpress coupon in some circumstances, which is of limited value if you no longer wish to shop on the platform.
7. The biggest risk isn't the clothing - it's the after-sales process.
My greatest disappointment wasn't that some items weren't suitable. It was the dispute process itself, which I found opaque, inconsistent and unnecessarily difficult despite making every effort to provide the requested evidence and resolve matters professionally with both the sellers and AliExpress. In my experience, the process eventually reached a point where there was no meaningful opportunity to discuss or clarify the issues further, even though I still had additional evidence and unanswered questions. I was left feeling that the process had become procedural rather than focused on achieving a fair outcome.
8. This experience changed my buying behaviour.
I have purchased many items through other online marketplaces and have always found the returns process straightforward, transparent and customer-focused. This experience with AliExpress has had the opposite effect. Rather than building confidence in the platform, it has reinforced my preference to shop elsewhere. Price is important, but trust, fairness and responsive customer service are ultimately what determine where I choose to spend my money.
My conclusion
Based on this experience, I will not purchase through AliExpress again. If you do choose to buy, do so knowing that you may waste your money and have nothing to show for it. Even though I demonstrated strong evidence, all my time and efforts got me nowhere. So by all means, take screenshots of every product listing, keep all correspondence and photograph every item as soon as it arrives – but know this may get you nowhere. I hope your experience is better than mine, but I believe buyers should understand the risks & potential difficulties of the returns and dispute process before ordering. 

Further Update – 23 Jul 2026
AE did email me - invited questions, ignored my reply, no way to upload evidence, then closed my appeal for missing the deadline.

title: Defective Products, Terrible Quality Control & One of the Worst Return Experiences I've Ever Had!!
text:
I have spent over 10 hours, sent more than 50 emails, and travelled to six different return locations trying to return products that should never have been shipped in the first place.

The reason for my return wasn't that I changed my mind.
The clothing arrived with incorrect sizing, poor workmanship, unfinished construction, and obvious quality issues. Some items looked like they had never been properly finished before being packaged. The sizing was nowhere close to what was advertised, making several items completely unwearable. These are quality control failures that fall entirely on SHEIN.
Instead of standing behind the products they sell, SHEIN leaves customers to deal with the consequences.

The customer service has been just as disappointing as the products. After more than 50 emails, I continue receiving the same generic copy-and-paste responses that completely ignore the concerns I've raised. Not once has anyone meaningfully addressed the poor quality of the items, the incorrect sizing, or the countless hours I've spent trying to return them.
The biggest issue has been SHEIN's return process in Toronto.

I previously completed a SHEIN return while I was in Vancouver, where the return was handled through Canada Post. It was simple, professional, and took only a few minutes. That's exactly how a return process should work.My experience in Toronto has been the complete opposite.

SHEIN uses a third-party return network that has been an absolute nightmare. I have been sent from location to location, only to find businesses that were closed, difficult to access, or operating with extremely limited hours. One designated return location had nothing more than a handwritten piece of paper taped to the door listing its business hours. I took photographs because I couldn't believe a company the size of SHEIN expects customers to rely on a return network operating like this.
I work full-time and don't permanently live in Toronto. Spending days travelling across the city trying to return defective clothing is completely unreasonable. I've documented every trip, every location, walking directions, screenshots, emails, and photographs because I simply couldn't believe how difficult this process became.

No customer should have to spend weeks chasing down return locations because a company shipped merchandise that failed basic quality standards.

The most frustrating part is the complete lack of accountability. Instead of acknowledging the problems or offering a practical solution, SHEIN continues sending automated responses while the customer absorbs all of the time, inconvenience, and expense.

A return policy is supposed to protect customers when products arrive defective or not as described. It should not become a second job.

If SHEIN can provide a simple, efficient return process through Canada Post in one Canadian city, there is no reason customers in another city should be forced through such a disorganized and inaccessible third-party network.

This entire experience has shown me that once something goes wrong, customer service and accountability disappear. I expected far better from a global retailer.

I sincerely hope SHEIN reviews both its quality control and its Canadian return process because no customer should have to fight this hard to return products that should never have passed inspection in the first place.
I will not be shopping with SHEIN again, and I cannot recommend them based on this experience.

On June 10, 2026, I placed an order for a total of $496.49 USD. Days passed, and I noticed the order was still marked as "pending payment," and I couldn't even see all the items from my purchase. I contacted support to ask what was going on, and they told me I had to contact my bank because they had no record of any payment related to that order. Even though I sent them proof of payment, they kept insisting they hadn't received anything. I contacted my bank, and they confirmed the payment went through successfully; I could also see it marked as "completed" in my banking app.

I went back to Shein support, and this time they told me I should open a dispute/chargeback with my bank since they hadn't received the money. Once I filed the dispute, support suddenly changed their story and said they did see the payment and that it was linked to my order. I told them that was fine and to please just process what I ordered. After some time, they asked me to confirm the payment by uploading the receipt through a link. I did this about 5 times until they finally told me the payment was confirmed.

However, a few days later, I saw the purchase was still pending. I contacted Shein support again, and now they claim that because the payment is under dispute, they cannot process my order. Mind you, it was their own support team that told me to open the dispute in the first place because they claimed they didn't have the money! Now they refuse to process it because of the dispute.

I was furious, but I honestly thought Shein was trustworthy and wouldn't engage in these kinds of dirty tactics. $496 might be a lot to me, but it's nothing to a massive company like Shein. They keep sending automated messages even when I'm supposedly talking to a human, acting as if I'm bothering them. Finally, my bank confirmed that the dispute was officially closed. ​Banned Practice #6 ("Bait-and-Switch"): It is illegal to promote a specific product at a specific price (or for free) if the business actually intends to substitute it with a different requirement or force you into a different commercial transaction (like buying other goods to "unlock" it).

I seemed to be one of the few people who wasn’t using Temu despite its relentless advertising. Eventually, I signed up in April, thinking I’d give it a fair chance. Unfortunately, purchasing fashion garments from Temu has been one of the most disappointing online shopping experiences I’ve had.

What made the experience even worse was Temu’s response. After I complained about one of the misleading products, I was offered a $3 no-return refund. Rather than resolving the issue, it felt dismissive and disrespectful. A responsible marketplace should hold sellers accountable for deceptive listings instead of allowing misleading advertisements to continue while customers absorb the disappointment.

I’m now waiting for my final order to arrive, after which I’ll be deleting my Temu account permanently. Consumers deserve honesty, accurate product descriptions, and products that reasonably match the images used to market them. In my experience, Temu has failed to provide that standard.

I hope Temu begins enforcing stricter quality control and takes stronger action against sellers who misrepresent their products. Until then, I cannot recommend the platform for purchasing clothing.

If Temu is a Chinese company, this kind of behavior reflects poorly on a government that claims to take a strong stance against theft and fraud.

I would urge others to be extremely careful with this app — take screenshots of your cart before checking out, and monitor your bank account closely after any order.
